pr_title: Coerce uid and gid to integer to prevent failures in Windows.
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Pete Higgins <pete@peterhiggins.org>

Fixes #10454.

There doesn't appear to be a valid usecase for a uid or gid that is not an integer string, ie `uid "pete"`. 

Running the test script in the linked issue after this PR:

```
PS C:\vagrant\chef> ruby -Ilib chef-bin\bin\chef-apply .\test_user_uid.rb
Recipe: (chef-apply cookbook)::(chef-apply recipe)
  * windows_user[dude] action create
    - alter user dude
    - change uid from 1001 to 8019
```
pr_comments: Based on the test failures, I made some wrong assumptions in here. Will revisit.
I do have a fix for this, but I can't push to this branch anymore. I'll open a new one. 😅

issue_context.title: `no implicit conversion of FFI::MemoryPointer into Integer` when you specify `uid`
issue_context.body:
This seems a lot like this bug from forever ago: https://github.com/chef/chef/issues/4024

## Description
the `user` resource on windows blows up with `no implicit conversion of FFI::MemoryPointer into Integer` if you specify `uid`.

If you remove `uid`, then it works fine.

## Chef Version
15.9.7

## Platform Version
Windows 10

## Replication Case

```
user 'dude' do
  uid "8019"
end
```

And it will blow up.

## Client Output
<!--- The relevant output of the chef-client run or a link to a gist of the entire run, if there is one.

The debug output (chef-client -l debug) may be useful, but please link to a gist, or truncate it. -->

```
TypeError
---------
no implicit conversion of FFI::MemoryPointer into Integer

Resource Declaration:
---------------------
# In C:/chef/cache/cookbooks/fb_users/resources/default.rb

109:     user username do
110:       uid mapinfo['uid']
111:       # the .to_i here is important - if the usermap accidentally
112:       # quotes the gid, then it will try to look up a group named "142"
113:       # or whatever.
114:       #
115:       # We explicityly pass in a GID here instead of a name to ensure that      
116:       # as GIDs are moving, we get the intended outcome.
117:       unless node.windows?
118:         gid ::FB::Users::GID_MAP[pgroup]['gid'].to_i
119:       shell info['shell'] || node['fb_users']['user_defaults']['shell']
120:       manage_home manage_homedir
121:       home homedir
122:       comment mapinfo['comment'] if mapinfo['comment']
123:       password pass if pass
124:       end
125:       action :create

Compiled Resource:
------------------
# Declared in C:/chef/cache/cookbooks/fb_users/resources/default.rb:109:in `block (2 
levels) in class_from_file'

windows_user("someuser") do
  action [:create]
  default_guard_interpreter :default
  declared_type :user
  cookbook_name "fb_users"
  uid "8019"
end
```
comments: @jaymzh Any chance you can see if this is an issue on 16.6 as well?
Oh I hadn't seen this. Thanks!
Oh. If we `.to_i` it works. We should coerce this properly

review_comments: This allows setting uid and gid to nil or something coercible to Integer. I could preserve the existing error behavior by changing this to `coerce: proc { |n| n && Integer(n) rescue n }`, but there are many other places in resources where a `coerce: proc { |n| Integer(n) }` is used.
